prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 3: switch family entirely to a kernel method — SVC with an RBF kernel on standardised features — to generate a genuinely different ranking than the two boosting points already tried. Preprocessing: median impute (no missing values exist) plus standardisation, which this family requires. Hyperparameters: kernel='rbf', C=10.0, gamma='scale', class_weight left at default so the score is attributable to the ranking change alone. 2,760 training rows is far inside SVC's quadratic-in-rows budget (cost 5, but n is small), so runtime is a non-issue. I will read roc_auc, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut and cut_headroom against the two gbdt points to see whether the kernel ranking is above the 0.9369 best-cut ceiling seen so far; if it is, attempts 4-5 tune C<path> around it, if it is not, attempt 4 goes to a bagging family (extra_trees / random_forest, fully grown) as the last unexplored ranking generator.",
  "model_family": "kernel",
  "candidate_models": [
    "svc"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "kernel": "rbf",
    "C": 10.0
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "median",
    "scale": true,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "Model family changes from gbdt (hist_gbdt attempt 1, xgboost attempt 2) to kernel: svc with an rbf kernel. Preprocessing changes from scale:false to scale:true (mandatory for a distance<path> method); impute stays median, no missingness columns. No boosting hyperparameters carried over — C=10.0 and gamma='scale' are new; class_weight stays default, so nothing on the operating-point axis moved and the whole difference is the ranking generator.",
  "rationale": "The Critic's verdict is wrong_model_family: attempt 2 cut train_val_gap 0.0689→0.0500 without the validation ranking following (roc_auc 0.9788→0.9763), so variance is no longer the binding constraint and another point in boosting space would buy nothing. cut_headroom is 0.0067–0.0074, only ~17% of the 0.0442 still needed, so class_weight and any operating-point move are bounded far below the bar — the remaining distance is on the ranking axis, which means the family or the features, and features cannot be derived here. Of the families never tried, an RBF-SVC is the one whose decision surface differs most from axis-aligned tree splits: spambase's 57 continuous, heavily skewed frequency columns are standardised into a space where a smooth kernel boundary can express the diffuse many-small-signals structure that trees approximate with staircases, and rbf-SVC is a well-documented strong performer on this specific dataset. C=10 with gamma='scale' gives a moderately flexible boundary without the near-memorisation seen in attempt 1; 2,760 rows keeps the quadratic fit well under the 600 s / 2 GB budget. This is the largest single ranking-axis change still available in one attempt, and it leaves bagging (extra_trees<path>) as a clean fallback for attempt 4.",

  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 3
}
